name: Airfloa Rail Technology Limited
sector: Railway coach interiors and engineering systems
summary: Airfloa designs and supplies railway coach interiors, equipment and engineering systems. Its revenue expansion and railway qualification are real strengths, but growth has not yet translated into dependable owner cash. FY26 parent revenue was ₹319.60 crore and PAT ₹39.15 crore, while operating cash flow was negative ₹57.45 crore. At the dated 19 October secondary close of ₹501.20, issued equity is valued at ₹1,201.37 crore, about 30.69 times group owner earnings. The next expansion combines working capital, infrastructure, capitalized development and proposed investments whose available financing is not independently established. This is a financing-sensitive growth/special-situation research watchlist, not an evidence-backed compounder or an actionable purchase conclusion. Verified collections, an executable funding bridge and disciplined deployment would matter more than another order headline. BQS is 4.8; GQS is capped at 5.0; IAS is NS. [S1,S6,S9,S13]

MOAT.reason: Rail qualification and turnkey engineering relationships are useful, but concentration and named competing suppliers constrain pricing power. Margin contraction despite scale is contrary evidence to a strong moat.

DUR.reason: Existing railway order access supports a runway; consortium allocation, government ordering, technology qualification and proposed acquisition funding constrain accessible growth. Bid pipelines are not orders.

CAP.reason: Average capital returns are adequate, but incremental efficiency fell from about26.8% to9.1% against an analyst11–14% cost-of-capital range. Future development/JV economics remain unproved, not automatically valuable.

CASH.reason: Multi-year cash conversion is negative and large receivables/advances absorb funds. Claimed post-year-end collections and better inventory days are contrary evidence, but not audited proof that conversion recovered.

BAL.reason: Moderate reported debt/equity masks little ordinary cash and substantial planned investment/working-capital needs. The prior IPO and management financing claims are positives, but the linked growth paths need more finance.

EXEC.reason: Strong actual revenue delivery and new LOA are positives. Cash-collection promises, machinery deployment and new-technology commitments are not yet demonstrated; a proposal is not a completed integration.

EARN.reason: Operating earnings and ending-share EPS improved, but IPO dilution, historical normalization and future capitalized development costs make quality mixed. FY2026 other income is small and inventory change is an expense, contrary to a one-off-led profit claim.

R.reason: No base path is funded by independently established available finance. Hypothetical equity-rescue returns are sensitivities, not a supported investable base IRR.

D.reason: A conditionally financed bear path loses about87% of terminal share value; withdrawal/collection shocks enlarge funding needs. This supports severe downside, not a current default assertion.

L.reason: Historical capacity alone starts at9, but a dated LTASM-I signal lacks current primary stage/removal confirmation. That specific material restriction gap, not merely lack of live depth, prevents a final L.

GQS.cap_reason: Persistent poor cash realization, not merely one transient build.

ranking_eligibility.reason: Quality factors supported at Medium confidence with conditional gates. Investment ranking awaits supported funding and current BSE implementation evidence.

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
Airfloa Rail Technology Limited, BSE SME 544516/AIRFLOA, ISIN INE0XBS01012; formerly Air Flow Equipments (India) Private Limited. Cutoff: 20 October 2026, UTC. Price: ₹501.20, 19 October dated secondary BSE close, not a live executable quote. Actual shares: 23,969,954; market capitalization ₹1,201.3741 crore. Indian GAAP Accounting Standards under Section 133, not assumed Ind AS. FY26 consolidated accounts are the valuation opening perimeter; historical parent cash and PAT are paired, with the small subsidiary separately reconciled. All amounts are ₹ crore unless specified. Five modeled financial years FY27–FY31 end 31 March 2031, approximately 4.44 years after the valuation date; no interim dividends. Equity hurdle 15% nominal before personal tax; 12%/18% sensitivities. Analytical cost-of-capital range 11–14% is separate. Liquidity reference is ₹5 lakh, not a recommended position. [S1,S2,S13,S14]

G1 Integrity: Conditional because repeated compliance shortcomings and proposed deployments require monitoring, not because diversion is established. G2 Reliability: Conditional: FY26 audited statements are usable, but original/restated historical vintages must not be mixed, and the separately linked subsidiary pack is FY25. G3 Funding: Conditional: expansion is not demonstrably funded by current available facilities; an unfunded analyst growth case is not proof of current issuer default. G4 Tradability: Conditional because a dated secondary LTASM-I signal lacks a current primary stage/removal check. Input confidence is Medium on historical financials, governance and capital economics; Low on current unused financing, current BSE restrictions and a funded shareholder-return case. Overall investment confidence is Low; forecast uncertainty is High even where retrieved inputs have Medium confidence. [S1,S2,S6,S16,S17]

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
Canonical scores: GOV 4, MOAT 5, REV 8, DUR 6, CAP 5, CASH 2, BAL 3, EXEC 5, EARN 5. BQS contributions are 0.80 + 1.00 + 0.96 + 0.60 + 0.60 + 0.20 + 0.24 + 0.40 = 4.80, with 100% coverage. GQS contributions are 3.20 + 1.20 + 0.75 + 0.75 + 0.20 = 6.10 raw, capped at 5.00 for persistent poor cash realization. This is not a penalty for a single expansion year. No governance or funding-failure numeric override is applied. [E2,E3,E4,E6,E7,E8,E9,E10,E12]

IAS components: Q 4.80, R NS, D 2, P 4, L NS. Known weighted contribution is 2.00; coverage 55%; missing-data mathematical bound 2.45–6.50. There is no midpoint score or renormalization. R is unavailable because no independently supported financing plan funds the base path; L is unavailable because the specific surveillance issue is unresolved. D is scoreable from verified opening claims and explicit severe sensitivities, with Medium evidence confidence but High forecast uncertainty. Quality scores may be compared conditionally; IAS is not ranking eligible. Moving GOV and CAP by one point each changes BQS by up to 0.32 and raw GQS by 0.15; the cash-conversion cap remains 5.0. The structured factor ledger preserves each reason, contrary evidence and source linkage.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
The business combines design, manufacture, assembly and installation of coach interiors and rail-related systems rather than a recurring software or consumer franchise. Railways and their production ecosystem dominate demand: the FY26 annual report says the largest client accounts for more than ₹300 crore and over 90% of revenue. Billing, inspection, acceptance and collection timing therefore matter as much as order intake. Revenue is recognized before all cash is collected; March receivables of ₹214.02 crore illustrate the financing consequence. Separate product/geography price-volume bridges were not sufficiently disclosed to assign precise organic growth components. [S1,S2]

Sree Dakssnaa Aerospace and Defence India Private Limited was incorporated on 11 June 2024 and is 79.2% owned. FY26 AOC-1 reports assets ₹3.1466 crore, liabilities ₹0.1550 crore, nil revenue and loss ₹0.0052 crore; nil turnover does not mean nil costs or assets. Parent investment ₹0.0099 crore and the minority capital/premium explain the small group equity differences. The related customer-advance elimination is not treated as extra group cash. The website subsidiary pack examined is FY25, so the FY26 AOC-1/group notes, rather than a nonexistent separately verified FY26 pack, define the usable scope. [S1,S17]

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
Qualification, engineering capability, execution experience and an established rail customer relationship create useful entry friction. They do not establish unrestricted pricing power: public procurement, customer concentration, competitor qualification and project working capital constrain economics. FY26 core EBITDA margin is about 20.10%, below roughly 25.11% in the preferred FY25 restated parent series despite higher revenue. That is contrary evidence to a claim that scale automatically expands margins. [S1,S2]

Three directly relevant primary comparators were inspected: Oriental Rail supplies seats, berths and related coach materials; Hindustan Fibre Glass Works designs, manufactures and installs mechanical/electrical coach interiors and exteriors. Kineco designs and manufactures composite coach panels and offers turnkey interiors. These demonstrate contestable overlap, not identical businesses. Their product pages do not establish comparable current valuations or superior audited capital returns, so no fabricated three-company multiple table or market-share rank is used. Broader rolling-stock manufacturers are not clean substitutes for Airfloa's interior-system economics. MOAT 5 recognizes qualifications without awarding a monopoly premium. A stronger score requires sustained bid economics, repeat wins, warranty performance and cash-adjusted returns through a procurement cycle. [S18,S19,S22]

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
The six revenue observations are FY21 ₹121.8330 crore, FY22 ₹137.4938 crore, FY23 ₹95.1739 crore, FY24 ₹119.3036 crore, FY25 ₹192.3870 crore and FY26 ₹319.5976 crore. Annual additions are +₹15.6608 crore, −₹42.3199 crore, +₹24.1297 crore, +₹73.0834 crore and +₹127.2106 crore. Five-year CAGR is 21.27%; three-year CAGR from the weaker FY23 base is 49.75%. The five-year window was selected before scoring and earns REV 8 without a single-quarter uplift. FY21/22 are original annual disclosures; FY23–25 use IPO-restated parent accounts; the revenue series and profit-restatement limits are kept distinct. Ten-year comparable history is not established. [S1,S2,S3,S4]

The July 14 operating update reports provisional, unaudited Q1 FY27 revenue ₹100.7 crore versus ₹33.6 crore and a June order book of ₹433.8 crore. It does not supply reviewed quarterly PAT or CFO, and is not annualized into a TTM. Management's June call targeted FY27 revenue around ₹500 crore and a 12–13% PAT margin. The analyst base uses ₹465 crore, with ₹500 crore only in the bull path. The October 12 ₹34.85 crore ICF design/mock-up LOA is a consortium total with Blue Engineering, a 12-month execution period and Airfloa as lead; the entire amount is not automatically Airfloa-only revenue. Bid pipeline, MOUs and the proposed KIN order book are not added to signed revenue. [S6,S8,S10,S11]

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
Existing railway orders and engineering qualifications provide accessible demand, but a unit/capacity-to-revenue bridge sufficient to validate every five-year forecast is unavailable. The annual model is therefore an explicit financing diagnostic, not a fully underwritten capacity forecast. Base revenues are ₹465/558/658.44/750.62/840.70 crore in FY27–31; bull ₹500/675/843.75/1,012.50/1,164.38 crore; bear ₹360/360/378/396.90/416.75 crore. No KIN or new technology-JV sales are assumed. [S1,S6,S8,S10]

Management discussed FY27 infrastructure spend ₹30–35 crore, FY28 ₹30–40 crore and capitalized R&D of 8–9% of revenue. The base uses infrastructure ₹32.5/35/25/25/25 crore and R&D 8/7/6/5/5% of sales; bull and bear paths vary both. Five crore of BBBS CCDs was already paid against an up-to-₹25 crore plan; the model reserves the remaining ₹20 crore in FY27 without inventing investment income or terminal value. Possible overlap between R&D and JV spending is separately tested, not silently double-counted as certainty. The ₹48 crore proposed KIN transaction remains subject to diligence, approvals and definitive documentation; a separate all-cash stress adds its cost without speculative earnings. [S1,S6,S8]

Actual opening operating working capital is ₹255.93 crore. Incremental needs are 55%/45%/75% of positive revenue additions in base/bull/bear; these are forecast sensitivities, not ratios imposed backward on the opening balance. The model does not release the historical receivable stock merely to make growth financeable. Mixed incremental returns, negative cumulative cash conversion and unproved development economics explain why GQS is 6.1 raw but only 5.0 final. [S1,S2]

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
The FY26 statutory audit opinions are unmodified and audit-trail operation is reported. These positives do not erase the separate secretarial findings: a one-day related-party disclosure delay with ₹5,000 paid, incomplete website items, delayed forms, and MGT-14 filings for specified borrowing modifications still unfiled at the report date. Historical AGM/cost-audit compounding fees of ₹0.05 crore were reported paid. The IPO restatements disclose corrections including gratuity, statutory/MSME interest, CSR, interest, tax and asset write-offs. These are reporting and compliance deficiencies; they are not evidence here of intentional misstatement, diversion or fraud. [S1,S2]

The 20 July revised disclosure reports that Regional Director orders dated 13 July enhanced company CSR penalties for FY20–FY23 to ₹1.8007936 crore in total, from approximately ₹0.9004 crore. The company stated an intention to approach the Madras High Court. A filed writ, stay or relief was not verified; the annual report's older pending-appeal description is therefore not the latest procedural position. Directors' separate penalties are not charged to company cash in this model. Disclosed GST disputes total ₹0.7827598 crore; their existence is not a finding of a final adverse outcome. [S7,S1]

The board contains four family directors and two independent directors. March principal-promoter holdings total about 54.2%; a current encumbrance clearance was not established. Disclosed related-party items include ₹4 crore outstanding to Raghavendra and ₹2.10 crore capital purchases from Starkeon; their disclosure is not proof of misuse. Allocation discipline remains a live question because substantial cash is tied in customers/vendors while new technology and acquisition plans compete for finance. [S1,S2]

Promises versus delivery: September 2025 IPO proceeds partly deployed, but ₹10.767 crore equipment allocation remained unused at both March and June 2026; completion/commissioning must be distinguished from spending. June 3 management said about 20% of receivables had been collected by May-end and expected about 70% by June; a reconciled June collection statement was not verified. FY27 ₹500 crore revenue guidance has one strong provisional quarter, not a full-year outcome. The BBBS/technology venture remains investment/development work, while KIN remains proposed. These mixed milestones support EXEC 5 rather than assuming either success or failure. [S1,S6,S8,S9,S10]

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
The full historical ledger below preserves original/restated scopes, balance sheets and formulas. Preferred parent revenue/PAT/CFO for FY23 are ₹95.1739/1.4936/10.0792 crore; FY24 ₹119.3036/14.2328/3.4632; FY25 ₹192.3870/25.5580/−4.4329; FY26 ₹319.5976/39.1522/−57.4524. Cash PPE/intangible capex is ₹2.0563/0.8989/5.6732/17.1542 crore, giving reported CFO-minus-capex proxies ₹8.0229/2.5643/−10.1061/−74.6066 crore. Capital advances, the ₹5 crore financial investment and financing payments are separately identified, not hidden in that proxy. Gross profit is ND because a reliable compatible product-cost split was not established. FY21/22 CFO is also ND, not invented. [S1,S2,S3,S4]

Four-year cumulative parent CFO is −₹48.3429 crore against ₹80.4366 crore PAT, or −0.6010x. Capex cannot explain negative CFO: the operating absorption is led by receivables and advances. March receivables ₹214.0159 crore imply closing sales-proxy days about 244, not the same measure as management's average-days commentary. Inventory is ₹72.40 crore and vendor advances ₹31.1604 crore. FY26 inventory-change expense is positive ₹7.4833 crore, versus a ₹20.4825 crore credit in FY25; there is no claim that FY26 profit was boosted by an inventory-change credit. Gross debt ₹68.3098 crore includes current maturities ₹1.4129 crore. March group cash ₹13.0822 crore contains ₹10.767 crore earmarked IPO equipment cash, leaving an upper bound ₹2.3152 crore ordinary cash before any additional liens or operating buffer. [S1,S2,S6,S9]

Restatement bridge: original FY23/FY24/FY25 parent PAT was approximately ₹0.4581/13.5115/25.7825 crore, versus IPO-restated ₹1.4936/14.2328/25.5580 crore. FY25 group original annual CFO −₹16.9436 crore is not interchangeable with IPO-restated group −₹4.4460 crore or FY26 annual parent comparative −₹2.8699 crore; interest/reclassification and subsidiary-capital presentation differ. The preferred historical ratio uses one identified parent series, while alternatives are retained. All observed FY25 CFO vintages remain negative, so weak conversion does not depend on selecting the worst vintage. [S1,S2,S5]

Core EBIT equals PBT + finance cost − other income. FY26 core EBIT ₹60.7820 crore and EBITDA ₹64.2514 crore exclude ₹0.4744 crore other income. FY24 other income included ₹3.1314 crore creditor write-back; normalized operating returns exclude all other income rather than capitalizing it. At 26% analytical operating tax, NOPAT is ₹21.3712/33.8709/44.9787 crore for FY24/25/26. Invested capital, equity + debt − reported cash − financial investments, is ₹118.1101/164.8055/287.0024 crore. FY26 average-capital return is 19.91%, but incremental NOPAT divided by additional IC is 9.09%, down from about 26.8% in the preceding step. Using total cash makes this diagnostic generous; restricted-cash adjustment would reduce the apparent efficiency. IPO timing and immature development assets limit causal interpretation. CAP 5 reflects mixed returns against an 11–14% analytical cost-of-capital range. [S1,S2]

Opening-claim map: operating WC includes inventory, receivables, other operating assets and deposits, less trade payables and ₹12.6776 crore recurring other liabilities. Tax/refund assets ₹1.3883 crore are removed and receive no separate cash recovery. Net current tax payable ₹13.1765 crore is already net of advance tax/TDS/TCS and is settled once; it is not offset again. Interest payable ₹0.077 crore, short gratuity ₹1.2254 crore and capital advance received ₹4.5 crore are paid once outside WC. The noncurrent gratuity ₹0.7542 crore remains a terminal claim. Current debt maturities are already in debt, not charged twice. The ₹3.2809 crore property advance receives no speculative recovery; paid BBBS CCDs receive no terminal cash uplift. Ordinary recurring statutory/employee/expense balances remain consistently in opening and forecast WC, with accelerated settlement tested separately. [S1]

FY26 group owner PAT is ₹39.1481 crore, total group PAT ₹39.1470 crore. Current-share EPS is about ₹16.33, not the reported weighted-average ₹18.66. Relative to FY25 restated owner PAT and pre-IPO ending shares, ending-share EPS rises only about 12%, far less than aggregate profit growth. Software addition ₹8.40 crore with only ₹0.0145 crore current amortization makes forward development amortization economically important; the model uses 20% opening-book development amortization plus a half-year charge on new additions, rather than perpetuating the low reported charge. This is a declining-book economic proxy, not a verified straight-line asset schedule. No inference of improper capitalization is made merely from this timing difference. [S1,S2]

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
The dated close implies market capitalization ₹1,201.37 crore and FY26 group-owner P/E 30.69x. A cash-constrained EV cross-check adds ₹68.3098 crore debt and ₹0.6223 crore minority interest, subtracting only ₹2.3152 crore ordinary cash, not earmarked cash or unproved investment recoveries: approximately ₹1,267.99 crore, or 19.73x core EBITDA. This is a convention-sensitive cross-check, not an independently observed enterprise value. Reported FCF is negative, so an attractive positive FCF yield cannot be asserted. [S1,S13]

The linked model starts at the actual March 2026 balance sheet and projects FY27–31. Base/bull/bear core EBITDA margins are approximately 19.5–20%/21.5–23%/15–16%; normalized tax 26%; financing rates 10%/9%/12.5%. Physical and development investment, incremental WC, opening claims and interest on additional debt are explicitly linked. A half-year draw convention solves interest and debt together; no immediate tax shield on new-draw interest is assumed. Exit operating-value multiples are 12x/16x/8x NOPAT. Debt, minority interest, unpaid noncurrent benefits and other retained claims are deducted; dividends are zero. The assumptions are analyst scenarios, not management guidance relabeled as fact. [S1,S6]

With no independently verified new available bank limit, all three reference paths are UNFUNDED mechanical sensitivities. Their peak funding needs including buffer are approximately ₹62.38 crore bear, ₹183.27 crore base and ₹199.47 crore bull. Raw terminal prices around ₹99.28/468.03/1,055.79 before an unknown recapitalization are NOT funded targets or actionable fair values; funded conditional IRRs are null. The model separately shows the terminal cash deficit as a claim, but subtracting a deficit is not a substitute for financing the path. [A1]

Management on June 3 described ₹60 crore sanctioned but undisbursed and another ₹60 crore expected/in principle, not verified cutoff liquidity. Even assuming the full ₹120 crore incremental facility, base and bull retain roughly ₹95.91/103.51 crore funding gaps including buffer. The bear is financeable only under that explicit facility assumption, with terminal price about ₹66.58 and annualized return −36.82%, approximately 87% terminal price loss. A ₹60 crore-only base retains about ₹139.59 crore gap. A hypothetical ₹200 crore gross equity issue, 5% costs, at ₹250/350/501.20 funds the base but dilutes the outcome: terminal prices about ₹356.39/383.83/407.50 and annualized returns −7.81%/−6.26%/−4.98%. No such issue is assumed announced. [S6,A1]

Base sensitivity with the assumed ₹120 crore facility: proposed KIN cash cost adds a gap to about ₹143.91 crore; full R&D/JV overlap reduces it to about ₹77.33 crore; incremental WC +15 percentage points raises it to ₹172.18 crore; margin −3 points to ₹166.67 crore; zero ordinary opening cash to ₹98.22 crore. Extra IPO equipment spending beyond the infrastructure budget raises the gap to ₹106.13 crore. The terminal margin/multiple grid is separately labeled exit-only and must not replace the fully linked margin stress. [A1]

Reverse algebra at 25x terminal P/E and 12% owner net margin, unchanged shares and 1% entry/exit friction requires terminal revenue about ₹675.73/759.87/851.92 crore for 12%/15%/18% annualized hurdles over 4.44 years. At 15%, owner PAT must be about ₹91.18 crore. These are mathematical expectations, not proof that the required capital can be financed without dilution. Because available financing and resulting shares are unresolved, no actionable entry-price range, final R or IAS is issued. [A1]

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The decisive thesis-break variable is cash collection relative to the capital required for railway execution. A procurement delay or customer acceptance dispute can slow collections while wages, vendors, capitalized development and debt costs continue. Customer concentration can then translate into refinancing dependence, deferred projects or dilution even with positive accounting profit. Qualification and the strong FY26/Q1 revenue record are the strongest evidence against a blanket business-failure thesis; they do not by themselves pay creditors. [S1,S6,S10]

The linked severe stress adds withdrawal of 25% of opening bank working-capital lines, losses on 10% of opening receivables/inventory and 20% of vendor advances to the no-new-bank-finance bear case. It produces a roughly ₹109.82 crore financing gap including buffer. The withdrawal reduces debt and its future interest once; it is not charged again at exit. The bear also settles the disclosed company CSR and GST exposures as an adverse outcome sensitivity, not as a prediction of legal defeat. Recovery from paid technology investments is not assumed. These paths support Severe capital-impairment risk at the stated price, with D 2, while G3 remains Conditional rather than an evidenced current default. [S1,S7,A1]

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: At unchanged shares, five times the current equity value is about ₹6,006.87 crore and ten times is ₹12,013.74 crore. At 25x owner earnings and a 12% net margin, those outcomes require PAT roughly ₹240.27/480.55 crore and revenue ₹2,002.29/4,004.58 crore. Dilution increases the required total business scale; these are not revenue forecasts. A lower terminal multiple makes the task harder. The five-year funding diagnostic already struggles at base terminal revenue ₹840.70 crore, so the proposed acquisition and a broad railway market narrative do not establish a financed route to either outcome. The designation is Speculative / unsupported, not impossible. Per-share returns depend on revenue, margin, share-count change and exit multiple together; large aggregate revenue growth alone is insufficient. [S1,S6,A1]

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
1. Collections: March receivables ₹214.02 crore; obtain the June/September ageing and cash bridge against the June collection promise. A failure to improve collections requires investigation; a large unprovided loss or inability to fund obligations would break the cash thesis.
2. Funding: distinguish the June ₹60 crore sanction claim, second ₹60 crore proposal, actual disbursements, covenants and unused limits. Base-case commitments exceeding executable resources, not merely a headline facility size, determine the funding warning.
3. IPO equipment: ₹10.767 crore unutilized at June. Verify deployment, commissioning, qualification and revenue separately; changes in objects or unexplained use require a governance review.
4. Development/BBBS: ₹5 crore paid, up to ₹25 crore plan; reconcile further payments, capitalization, ownership rights and amortization. Warning is cash deployment without milestone evidence, not the existence of R&D itself.
5. KIN: ₹48 crore proposed. Require definitive consideration, assumed liabilities, funding, closing and audited acquired economics before adding earnings. A materially larger cash obligation without resources would worsen G3.
6. Earnings quality: track owner EPS after dilution and software amortization, rather than only PAT growth. Margin erosion plus longer collection cycles is a linked stress signal.
7. Compliance: obtain CSR court/stay status, GST developments and completion of the reported MGT-14/website deficiencies. Distinguish procedural updates from final findings.
8. Trading: verify current BSE ASM stage/removal and executable depth; lot is 500 at cutoff, with announced reduction to 250 only from 16 November. Reassess actual-position implementation rather than assuming the ₹5 lakh proxy is suitable.
9. Concentration/order conversion: reconcile backlog, execution, cancellations and the consortium's attributable scope. One provisional quarter is not proof of durable diversified demand.
Review at the next signed results, material funding/acquisition disclosure or exchange restriction change. This is a research cadence, not an automated reminder. [S1,S6,S7,S8,S9,S10,S11,S15,S16]

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Insufficient evidence for an investable IAS; financing-sensitive growth/special-situation watchlist with mixed business quality and poor cash realization. BQS 4.8 and capped GQS 5.0 do not meet the compounder criteria. No matrix cell based on a fabricated IAS is assigned. Research priority is high because collections, financing and allocation updates can materially change the outcome, not because the current price is demonstrably cheap. A lower share price alone cannot cure an unfunded operating plan or unresolved implementation restrictions. A funded plan with actual draw terms, reconciled subsequent collections, controlled development/acquisition spending and verified BSE conditions would permit a fresh R/L/IAS assessment. Existing-holder conclusions require actual position size, liquidity, taxes and alternatives; this dossier is not an instruction to trade. [S1,S6,S13,S16]

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
Sources below distinguish issuer filings, mirrored signed primary documents, official offer/master records and secondary market/status data. The historical and scenario ledgers retain formulas and all opening claims. The June CRISIL IPO monitoring report corroborates the reported utilization/earmarking, but explicitly is not an audit or a bank credit-rating rationale. [S21] Annual-report bank-rating statements are attributed issuer claims: a current CRISIL bank-facility rationale was not independently retrieved. The August 2024 Infomerics issuer-not-cooperating rationale concerns an earlier rating relationship and is not proof of a current default or a replacement for a current agency opinion. A secondary lead for a September 2026 SMERA SME1 grading was not verified in its attachment and is not used; that scale must not be substituted for a bank-facility rating. [S1,S12]

Material open questions are actual September cash/collections, accessible unused borrowing and covenants, final KIN terms and funding, further BBBS/technology payments, full FY26 subsidiary notes, current promoter encumbrances, and current primary BSE surveillance. Historical original/restated differences remain visible rather than silently harmonized. The model assumes 26% operating tax, explicit reinvestment and draw costs, no dividends, no speculative investment recoveries and conservative separation of earmarked cash. These are transparent bounded diagnostics, not predictions with statistical confidence intervals. No current-default, diversion or fraud conclusion is inferred from the disclosed deficiencies or the model's funding gaps.

valuation.scope: Forward group diagnostics from March audited balances. New KIN business and speculative technology revenue excluded; FY26 subsidiary has nil turnover and small disclosed net assets. Full-year FY27 includes provisional Q1 sales but no fictitious October cash balance.
limitations: Bank draw, undrawn funded versus nonfund facilities and conditions are not independently verified. Management on June 3 said ₹60 crore was sanctioned but pending disbursement and another ₹60 crore was expected. No sanctioned headline is treated as observed cash.

Future research/development is cash reinvestment, even when capitalized. Development amortization uses 20% of opening book plus 10% of new cash additions, an analyst declining-book proxy rather than a verified straight-line asset schedule; no guaranteed project value is added. Infrastructure budgets include remaining IPO machinery rather than stacking it again. JV CCD cash is separate in reference; overlap sensitivity reduces it once.

No KIN income or ₹180 crore target order book is added. Acquisition-only sensitivity adds ₹48 crore cash without value/revenue and is deliberately a financing stress, not a complete deal valuation; taxes/costs could add more.

Existing working-capital facilities are assumed renewed except explicit withdrawal stress. Negative cash indicates model funding need, not actual default. Mechanical terminal prices cannot be acted on absent finance/dilution terms.

Ordinary operating liabilities receive consistent opening and forecast WC treatment. Separate accelerated payment is a timing stress with one restoration, not permanent arbitrary liquidation. Net current income tax is paid once; unidentified government balances and NBFC TDS refund are excluded from WC/recovery and not netted again.

Long gratuity remains an exit claim. New annual operating expenses assumed paid as part of EBITDA cash costs; no duplicated opening provisions. No fresh equity terms or share dilution invented. Existing CCD investment and property advances receive no separate cash recovery/terminal credit.
